Mkhwebane's last stand

By: Joy Summers | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Public Protector Busisiwe Mkhwebane has been humiliated yet again. In the most recent judgement against her, the courts found that she doesn’t understand the law, she fails to act rationally and ig

Unique Selling Point:
On camera interview with insider Free State PP Sphelo Samuals

Summary:
Mkhwebane has suffered defeats in every single one of the major reviews that have gone to court and by big margins too. These findings have been overwhelming in their reasoning and devastating in their rhetoric. All of them related to foundational, structural and institutional failures under Mkhwebane’s leadership, and they have all severely weakened the office of the Public protector.

Then Six days ago, Sphelo Samuals, the provincial head of the Public protector’s office in the Free State did something unprecedented. He wrote a letter to his boss on Public Protector stationery. It was entitled: “ Friendly request to resign.”

In the letter Samuals appealed to whatever sense of pride Mkhwebane had left and in order to save taxpayers money to resign. He alleges that she is pursuing personal and political agendas of her own, that she is costing the office a lot of money through her reckless litigation, and he agrees with the courts that she ‘lacks the basic knowledge of the law and its practical application” He also says that she has eroded the values and the principles that the office stands for and that staff morale is at an all-time low




Further information:
Mkwhebane acted quickly and immediately suspended him. We will send a formal interview request to her on Monday 16th March. But Samual’s letter is the second salvo. His first was a damning affidavit to parliamentary speaker Thandi Modise. In the affidavit he gives his background – an attorney that has been with the Office of the PP for twenty years. He further explains how he was attacked in his office by a complainant back in 2011 which ended with both himself and the complainant laying assault charges against each other. He was exonerated but now nine years later Mkhwebane wants him to face a disciplinary for assault and she says that is the reason for his claims and his claims in the 12 page affidavit accuse her of tyrannical management in the office and inculcating an environment of fear where people are too afraid to speak out for fear of being victimized.

But he is not alone and it appears that the end may be nigh for the Public protector as most of the major political parties, except the EFF have begun to call for her resignation. The DA have submitted over 7000 pages of evidence to support their motion to establish an ad hoc committee to remove her from office. But Mkhwebane is not taking that lying down and has gone to the courts to declare the actions of parliament to remove her, illegal.

In a hard hitting Carte Blanche we get the inside track of how the PP has been running her office, what legacy she will leave and how her staying or leaving will impact on our political landscape.

travel to Bloemfontein Joy and Derek

Script:


Public Protector and the insiders final script. TX Sunday 5th April 2020

Commentary One
Parliament has started proceedings that could remove Busisiwe Mkwhebane from office, but the public protector is defiant, and says she is not going anywhere until 2023, and she has gone to court to stop that process, before it even begins

On the eve of the lockdown I met with her spokesperson Oupa Segalwe

Derek Watts
Well parliament has started a process that could remove her from office, but she says that only God can remove her?
Oupa Segalwe
That is correct, but she is advised by her counsel the rules on the basis of which Parliament has embarked upon, and that process is unlawful and unconstitutional.

Commentary Two
But the public protector is against the ropes, her high-profile reports have been lambasted by the judiciary. Lawson Naidoo is executive secretary of the Council for the Advancement of the South African Constitution.

Lawson Naidoo CASAC
The quality of her reports in these high profile matters really calls into question her capacity to be able to do the job, her competence in being able to exercise the power- the immense power that the office of the public protector has.

Commentary Three
March brought the latest embarrassing judgement. In her report on the President’s CR17 campaign funds Mkhwebane accused him of misleading parliament, and said there was suspicion of money laundering. The judges disagreed.

Lawson Naidoo
What the court said, and this was a full bench of the Pretoria High Court, said that that there were no facts to back up many of her findings, and the court went so far as to say, that she lacked a basic knowledge of the law and the constitution

Commentary Four
But spokesperson Oupa Segalwe defends Mkhwebane. He says very few of her reports have been set aside by courts, and she is being unfairly targeted

Oupa Segalwe
I'm saying she has put out hundred and forty seven reports. Only four of those reports have been reviewed and set aside the rest of them have not. So what is that?
Derek
Well what is it?
Oupa:
It tells of bias on the part of those that are gunning for her.
Derek:
But Oupa the highest courts in the land accusing her of incompetence, falsehood and that she doesn't even understand the law?

Oupa Segalwe
Judge's comments are not findings. The court did not make a ruling of incompetency or that she has misconducted herself. That is not a finding, it's remarks. There's only one body that can make a finding of incompetence of incapacity of misconduct against the Public Protector and that is Parliament.

LINK
Then a few weeks ago, another substantial clue in the apparent turmoil in the public protector’s office, came in the form of this letter

Sphelo up sound
Dear advocate Mkhwebane, I am directing this request to you to resign your position as Public Protector

Commentary five
Free State provincial representative in the Public Protector’s office, Sphelo Samuel believes his boss, Busisiwe Mkhwebane must be stopped.

Sphelo up sound
I am making this request to appeal to whatever sense and pride is left in you, to save the taxpayers money with your continued reckless litigation that is costing this office a lot of money

Commentary six
For 20 years, Samuel says he gave his working life to the office of the Public Protector.
Now he accuses her of incompetence, unleashing tyranny in the office, and plunging it into financial ruin

Derek:
In the letter you say that you lack the basic knowledge of the law and its practical application, although that was quoting the full bench of the North Gauteng High Court.
Sphelo
And I believe they were right!

Commentary Seven
Samuel has now been suspended. He says Mkhwebane has dredged up an old case from 2011 and is using it to purge him. She denies that

Sphelo
Look I believe I believe her agenda is to destroy that office, and what better way to do that then to you know target the institutional memory of that office- the people that brought it to where it was

Derek:
But why would she tried to destroy the office that was holding the fort against state capture?
Sphelo:
Precisely to protect state capture and to see to it that the people implicated in state capture are protected.

Commentary eight
And those people he says, are former premier Ace Magashule and current MP Mosebenzi Zwane

LINK
While senior staff members have made serious allegations against her, the Public Protector questions why these claims have only emerged when they are facing disciplinary action

Commentary nine
Isaac Matlawe spent 12 years in the Pretoria office, ensuring reports done by the investigators used the correct laws to make their findings. He says Mkhwebane dismantled that structure and that may be why the report on the president, based its findings on the wrong laws.

Derek
Now Sphelo took a bold step. How do you see his actions?
Isaac
I fully agree with his assessment. I mean that office is deteriorating at an alarming rate

Commentary ten
Matlawe was suspended after raising issues of nepotism and maladministration. He resigned late in 2018 to pursue his career as an advocate. He too faced disciplinary action that he believes was a malicious attempt to ruin his new career

Derek
How do you see the immediate future for the PP?
Isaac
I think the honorable thing for her would just be to resign. I mean that office is suffering under her leadership

Commentary eleven
But Segalwe defends any claims that Mkhwebane wants to destroy the public protectors office

Derek:
More than one senior employee has come to us saying she wants to destroy the institution of public protector.
Oupa:
It's a strange claim that one because they are not again indicating how is she destroying it
Derek
Well they have, they have given us long interviews and affidavits

OUPA
Yes but those affidavits until they are proven, they mean very little. It’s their words against hers.

Commentary twelve
One of Samuel’s most serious allegations is that Mkhwebane is protecting senior politicians for their alleged role in the Vrede Dairy scandal, where millions of rands meant for poor farmers were diverted to Gupta linked companies

Sphelo
she said I would prefer that we not make any findings against politicians- for me it was key that we should.
Derek:
Are you saying it was as blatant as that?
Sphelo
Yes, yes, I am saying that. My belief is that she is protecting those politicians that are implicated. And that is Mr. Ace Magashule and Mr Mosebenzi Zwane

Commentary thirteen
Both politicians have denied any wrongdoing in the Vrede Dairy scandal. Casac also believes
Mkwhebane is dragging her feet on that investigation

Lawson Naidoo
Almost two years down the line she has yet to produce a report of that investigation, and she keeps deferring that matter, which again is an indication that the public protector is really not that keen to investigate the complicity of those key individuals

Commentary Fourteen
But, Segalwe says the public protector will produce written correspondence which will disprove those allegations against her

Derek Watts
So are you saying that the public protector will investigate Mr Zwane and Mr Magashule without fear or favour?

Oupa Segalwe
I'm saying that investigation is under way and those two among several others have already sat before her to answer questions in relation to that particular investigation, and there are no questions about whether or not the public protector exercises her powers impartially and without fear or favour or prejudice that that is what the Constitution expects of her and that's what she does.




Commentary Fifteen
Tebogo Kekana is an attorney and a star investigator who reported directly to Mkwhebane. Now he too is suspended, while his explosive affidavit tells a story of spies, the destruction of information, and the manipulation of facts to serve powerful political interests.

In December Kyle Cowen and Amabhungane broke his story

Kyle Cowan
And he speaks in this affidavit of State Security Agency spies’ officials essentially coming
into the office of the Public Protector and handing her the wording on a document for one of the remedial actions in her report.

Commentary Sixteen
And that remedial action was to nationalize the reserve Bank. The details of the case are complex but what is important about his affidavit is the allegation that spies gave the Public protector the wording to change the mandate of the Reserve Bank.

Kyle
The public protector was adamant that the Reserve Bank mandate had to be altered. It had to be nationalized. And now Tebogo explains in his affidavit okay, I cannot find a way legally to do this. She says don't worry we'll get an economist from the State Security Agency and they'll give us a solution. And that ends up being a nondescript little A4 piece of paper with the remedial action written on it

Commentary Seventeen
The public protector lost her case in the Reserve Bank/ Absa matter and was berated by the courts. Two years later Kekana’s affidavit reveals his despair at the charges levelled against him

Kyle Cowan
I think they're spurious. I think it's a ridiculous attempt to try and discredit a man who's got dirt on you. I think that Tebogo Kekana was with the public protector when she cooked this report and she knows that!

Commentary eighteen
But Segalwe says there was nothing untoward about the way Mkwhebane conducted that investigation

Derek
in Tebogo Kekana affidavit he claims that the state security agency and not the public protector wrote the report in the ABSA Bank matter.
Oupa
Mr. Kekana like Mr. Samuel only came up with those claims when he was facing disciplinary action for something else. The report he's referring to was issued in 2017. Why would he wait all these years and only come up with those claims now?



Commentary nineteen
But can all the whistleblowers be wrong? And what do we make of the damning judgements against Mkhwebane – are they wrong too? Now, when lockdown ends, it will be up to parliament to decide her fate.

Derek
Are you worried about your personal safety?
Sphelo
Yes. I am. But I refuse to live in fear. And if anything happens to me it happens. But the truth won’t be suppressed.

THE END 11 00 minutes

PROMO ONE
Tyranny, incompetence, no knowledge of the law – damning allegations by one of the Public Protectors most senior managers, but she says he is just disgruntled.

PROMO TWO
Another damning judgement against another report out of the office of the public protector. But Busisiwe Mkhwebane spokesman, says she only answers to parliament.

PROMO THREE
Will the Public protector lose her job? Parliament has started proceedings that could end with her removal. She says she is going nowhere. Expect fireworks after the lockdown.

metadata.Unique Selling Point: On camera interview with insider Free State PP Sphelo Samuals
metadata.Summary: Mkhwebane has suffered defeats in every single one of the major reviews that have gone to court and by big margins too. These findings have been overwhelming in their reasoning and devastating in their rhetoric. All of them related to foundational, structural and institutional failures under Mkhwebane’s leadership, and they have all severely weakened the office of the Public protector. Then Six days ago, Sphelo Samuals, the provincial head of the Public protector’s office in the Free State did something unprecedented. He wrote a letter to his boss on Public Protector stationery. It was entitled: “ Friendly request to resign.” In the letter Samuals appealed to whatever sense of pride Mkhwebane had left and in order to save taxpayers money to resign. He alleges that she is pursuing personal and political agendas of her own, that she is costing the office a lot of money through her reckless litigation, and he agrees with the courts that she ‘lacks the basic knowledge of the law and its practical application” He also says that she has eroded the values and the principles that the office stands for and that staff morale is at an all-time low
metadata.Further information: Mkwhebane acted quickly and immediately suspended him. We will send a formal interview request to her on Monday 16th March. But Samual’s letter is the second salvo. His first was a damning affidavit to parliamentary speaker Thandi Modise. In the affidavit he gives his background – an attorney that has been with the Office of the PP for twenty years. He further explains how he was attacked in his office by a complainant back in 2011 which ended with both himself and the complainant laying assault charges against each other. He was exonerated but now nine years later Mkhwebane wants him to face a disciplinary for assault and she says that is the reason for his claims and his claims in the 12 page affidavit accuse her of tyrannical management in the office and inculcating an environment of fear where people are too afraid to speak out for fear of being victimized. But he is not alone and it appears that the end may be nigh for the Public protector as most of the major political parties, except the EFF have begun to call for her resignation. The DA have submitted over 7000 pages of evidence to support their motion to establish an ad hoc committee to remove her from office. But Mkhwebane is not taking that lying down and has gone to the courts to declare the actions of parliament to remove her, illegal. In a hard hitting Carte Blanche we get the inside track of how the PP has been running her office, what legacy she will leave and how her staying or leaving will impact on our political landscape.
